idiom_name: Akka/Pekko Typed: sealed trait Command + ActorRef[Command]
implementation_notes: The idiomatic Scala command message is an actor protocol: a sealed trait Command with case classes sent to an ActorRef[Command], which gives a typed mailbox, single-threaded execution per actor and location transparency between local and remote refs; pattern matching on the sealed trait keeps handling exhaustive. Replies travel as an explicit ActorRef[Reply] field inside the command (the typed-actor convention) rather than through an implicit return channel. Without an actor runtime the same sealed trait plus a dispatcher works, but supervision, mailboxes, back-pressure and delivery guarantees then become your own code.
code_sketch:
sealed trait Command
final case class ReserveStock(orderId: String, qty: Int) extends Command
final case class CancelOrder(orderId: String) extends Command

val behavior: Behavior[Command] = Behaviors.receiveMessage {
  case ReserveStock(id, qty) => stock.reserve(id, qty); Behaviors.same
  case CancelOrder(id)       => stock.cancel(id); Behaviors.same
}
pitfalls: A non-persistent actor's mailbox is at-most-once: a command in flight during a restart is lost, so commands that must not be lost need Akka/Pekko Persistence or a broker.
Commands crossing an actor boundary must be immutable, and only serializable types can cross a remote boundary - sending a mutable collection or a non-serializable type fails late, at remoting time.
Blocking on a future inside receiveMessage stalls that actor's mailbox; use pipeToSelf or ask with the appropriate timeouts instead.
